courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introduction to World History: Middle Ages
courses.description: This course provides a broad survey of world history in the Middle Ages, with a particular focus on Europe and the Middle East. It shows how the medieval West inherited and built on the achievements of the ancient Greeks and Romans, becoming part of a wide, cosmopolitan world with well-established connections to Africa and Asia. Each week's lecture will explore a specific period and theme, after which students will have the chance to read samples of academic scholarship by experts on each topic and discuss related issues in conversation with classmates in tutorial sessions. By the end of the course, students will have a firm grasp of the basics of the medieval world and understand how the Western Middle Ages fit into the broader history of Eurasia in this period.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. To teach students the fundamentals of medieval world history: key dates, events, places, states, beliefs, innovations, etc.

2. To familiarise students with the most important debates and methodological approaches in medieval world history.

3. To help students develop the fundamental skillset and sensibility of a historian: how to understand primary sources, how to think critically about historical narratives, and how to effectively communicate their analysis to others.

1. 讓同學掌握西方中世紀的歷史梗概：關鍵日期、事件、地點、國家、信仰、科技發明。

2. 讓同學掌握史學界對中世紀的主要研究觀點和論辯。

3. 讓同學掌握歷史學家的技藝與敏銳觸覺：如何解讀原始史料、如何就歷史問題進行批判性思維、如何表達自己的觀點。

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Qin-Han China
courses.description: This course aims to study the major development of the first unitary empires in China, the Qin and the Han. Focus will be put on the changes of political, social and institutional patterns. Topics include significant political events, institutions of the central and the regional governments, social organization as well as the development of commerce and handicraft industries.
courses.learning_outcomes:
- Understand the discipline concepts of political history through the study of the history of Qin and Han empires.

- Develop critical thinking by examining some of the conventional wisdoms in the study of Chinese history.

- Grasp presentation skills through discussion in tutorials.

- Learn to use the solid knowledge of standard histories.

- 瞭解秦漢帝國的政治發展。

- 透過考察中國歷史的問題以培養批判思維。

- 透過導修課學習書面及口頭報告的技巧。

- 學習使用正史的知識。

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Ming China
courses.description: This course analytically presents the major national, political, social and cultural events during the period 1350-1683, from the outbreak of the late Yuan rebellion to the end of the nominal Ming regime in Taiwan. The establishment of important institutions and implementation of important policies, accounts of political incidents of far-reaching consequences, and literati performance in government and local society will be given special attention.
courses.learning_outcomes:
At the end of the course, students should be able to achieve the following objectives:

1. Gain a solid training in the craftsmanship of academic presentation and historiographical writing;
2. Identify, understand, and critically analyze major episodes and events in the history of the Ming dynasty;
3. Demonstrate profound understanding and critical analysis of various types of Ming historical archives.

學生完成課程後，將能：
1. 在作學術報告及寫作歷史學論文方面得到扎實的訓練；

2. 辨別、理解、及分析明朝歷史上的主要時段及重大事件；

3. 充分理解及深入分析各種明朝史料。

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Song, Liao, Jin, and Yuan
courses.description: This course aims to enhance students' understanding of the transition period from the tenth century to the fourteenth century in the Imperial China. Additionally, it provides students a comprehensive overview of key research questions in the historical study of Song, Liao, Jin and Yuan periods.
courses.learning_outcomes:
This course helps students to:

1) Perceive Song, Liao, Jin and Yuan history from a multi-national perspective.

2) Understand the fundamental concepts of Song political history.

3) Gain a basic knowledge of the characters of Liao, Jin and Yuan governance in China as Conquest Dynasties

4) The social and intellectual changes in the Song-Yuan transition

(一) 多強格局中的宋遼金元史

(二) 兩宋的基本「國是」與政治文化

(三) 遼、金、元作為征服王朝的基本特征與其中原政策

(四) 宋元之際的思想和社會轉變
courses.course_syllabus:
1) An Introduction to some basic research approaches concerning Song, Liao, Jin, and Yuan history

2) Exploring Song, Liao, and Xixia history from a multi-national perspective.

3) The foundation of the Northern Song Empire and its basic regulatory system

4) Strategic culture, military operations, and pacifism: military history from the Liao perspective

5) The great turn of political culture during the Major Reform

6) Song Huizong: an ambitious emperor

7) Cities and the urban culture of the Song China

8) Poltical characters of the Jin Dynasty and the North China in the twelfth century

9) Internal and diplomatic moves of the Southern Song Dynasty

10) The dual nature of the Mongol Empire as a Conquest Dynasty

11) Ethnical issues under the Mongol ruleship

12) Dowry: a fundamental change in the transition period from Song to Yuan

13) Imagined "Song Learning" and "neo-Confucianism"

14) Conclusive remark: the turning point of Chinese history--Tang-Song transition or Song-Yuan-Ming transition?

第一講: 宋遼金元史的基本研究面向與進路

第二講: 國際關係視野中的「宋－遼－西夏」史

第三講: 宋初開國規模與北宋中期國是問題

第四講: 戰略文化、攻守之勢與弭兵論: 遼史角度的軍事史

第五講: 熙豐新政與政治文化轉向

第六講: 藏在史書迷霧中的宋徽宗

第七講: 十二、十三世紀的城市與市民文化

第八講: 金朝之政治構成與十二世紀中葉的華北社會

第九講: 南宋的內務與外交

第十講: 從蒙古帝國到中原之主

第十一講: 蒙元統治下的中國社會與族群問題

第十二講: 奩中物—宋元社會史脈絡中的一條重要線索

第十三講: 想像的「宋學」與「新儒學」

第十四講: 中國歷史的轉折點: 唐宋還是宋元?

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Ancient China
courses.description: This course will give a brief introduction to the new discovery of ancient China in the light of archaeological theories and materials. Focus will be put on the regional interactions from prehistory to the pre-Qin periods. It is hoped that through this course students can gain a basic knowledge of the ancient Chinese history from an archaeological perspective. This course would be invaluable for anyone interested in Chinese antiquities and Chinese views on the formation of their own civilization.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Early Medieval China (200s - 590s CE)
courses.description: This course examines the development of Chinese history in the early medieval period (200s - 590s CE) from various aspects, including politics, military, ethnicity, religious beliefs, and intellectual trends, to analyze its significance as a transition period between two models of empire in Chinese history. It further adopts a comparative perspective to study the significance of the period in a world historical context. In addition, it also provides a survey of the state-of-arts in the field as a base for advanced research.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Understand the history of early medieval China in various aspects, including politics, economy, military, and culture, etc.

2. Learn the different definitions of medievality of China in Sinological context.

3. Analyze the dynamics of social development in early medieval China.

4. Develop a comparative perspective of reading the history of early medieval China in a world historical context.

5. Acquire critical and analytical skills of reading historical sources.

1. 從政治、經濟、軍事和文化等多元角度認識魏晉南北朝的歷史發展

3. 學習分析該時期社會發展的動力

4. 培養以比較史和世界歷史的視野以了解魏晉南北朝時期的中國歷史

5. 訓練以批判性與分析性的技巧研讀歷史資料

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Warfare in the Medieval West
courses.description:
'War, comrades, is a great locomotive of history.'- Leon Trotsky (1922)

From the beginning of recorded history, states, rulers, and warlords have resorted to violent conflict in order to enforce their will on others. Nonetheless, while war has been a constant fact of life for human society, the methods of war have changed greatly over time. Wars have also driven immense changes in human society itself, often far beyond the original intentions of political and military leaders. This dynamic has had a powerful effect on the history of the Western world, shaping the development of Western states as we know them today.

This course will introduce students to the military history of the medieval West (c. AD 500-1500), focusing on Europe and surrounding regions of North Africa and Western Asia. Through weekly lectures, readings, and discussions, you will learn about key developments in military technology and tactics, as well as the decisive wars and battles in which they were put to the test.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Learn the basic facts and details of Western military history in the period c. AD 500-1500.
2. Understand how changes in medieval Western societies drove changes in military strategy and tactics, and vice-versa.
3. Develop the fundamental skillset and sensibility of a historian: how to understand academic arguments, think critically about historical narratives, and effectively communicate an analysis to others.

1. 同學將能夠掌握公元六世紀至十六世紀這一千年的歐洲軍事歷史的梗概。

3. 同學將掌握歷史學者的重要技巧與觸覺：如何理解史學界的相關論辯、如何分析和批判歷史敘述、如何有效地表達自己的觀點。

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of the United States
courses.description: This course discusses topics on American modern history and its interpretation. Contents may change, depending on the teacher's emphasis in the term concerned. The focus may shift from the situation prior to World War II to the post-war development.
courses.learning_outcomes: As befits the course’s thematic approach, its readings will give voice to many scholarly perspectives and will engage with a variety of primary sources that should be viewed as historical texts that open windows onto inquiries into the nature of class, gender, minority status, immigration, foreign relations, religion, technology, and culture. With our emphasis on critical thinking, essay writing, and primary source interpretation, not only will students be profoundly better informed as to the subject matter and demonstrably more expert on matters of historical investigation; you will also leave with an enhanced set of skills. After successfully completing the coursework, students will be better able to express ideas clearly in writing, to conduct scholarly research, to analyze information and to critique differing viewpoints, to compare and to contrast contrary cases of historical interpretation, to discern and to explain the links between historical events, and to assess the importance of historical documents or of cultural artifacts whether they comprise a political cartoon, book, painting, speech, song, or film.
courses.course_syllabus:
Our course will stand true to its name and explore modern American history rather than recount it. We will take a thematic rather than a progressive line of inquiry and essentially sacrifice the comforts of an orderly timeline for the challenges of a non-linear exploration. Chronology will not be eliminated as the lectures will roughly flow from the eighteenth through the twentieth centuries and the events and the movements we investigate will be placed in their temporal contexts, but we will be most interested in the links between different periods with regards to specific subjects. The weekly lecture topics include economics; territorial expansion; popular movements that originated outside government structures and the influence they later wielded within them; the betrayal, confrontations, and confinement of Native Americans; slavery and institutionalized bigotry; religion and popular culture; urban development; the causes of and responses to economic impoverishment; international relations; and crises of authority. For example, we will consider what the country’s “Founding Fathers” meant by their declaration of each individual’s right to the “pursuit of happiness,” and how that resulted in a clique of late nineteenth century “Robber Barons.”

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Japan
courses.description: This course explores the history and culture of Japan from the ancient time to the present. It covers the aspects of political and economic development, foreign relations, social thought, cultural feature, historical site and various typical literature of Japan in different periods. Through this course, students will gain a thorough understanding of the cultural evolution of Japan which was greatly influenced by the cultures of China, Europe and the U.S. successively, and the interactions among the developments of politics, society and literature in Japan. They will also be able to command the prospect of Japan and the Japanese culture in the 21st century. This course is interactive in nature. Lessons will be conducted in the forms of PowerPoint demonstration, multi-media learning (watching history film, documentary, TV program, drama, song and dance, music program and the Internet entertainment, etc), appreciation of photos of historical site and relic, selective reading of the traditional and pop literature, class discussion, interactive tutorial and e-learning modules.

courses.title: History of Korea
courses.description: This course introduces and examines the historical development of Korea over the past 2,000 years up to the present. It covers the imperial era comprising the periods of Three Kingdoms, Koryo Dynasty, and Chosen Dynasty, which ended in 1910 when Japan annexed Korea, the period of Japanese colonialism, independence movement and Korean War, and subsequently the separation between South and North Koreas, each of which has experienced extremely divergent pathways of development since the 1950s. The course also analyzes and discusses major factors that affecting the transformation of Korea over different stages of historical development.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. The students can trace and analyze the historical development of Korea and explain the factors that affecting its historical development.

2. The students will be able to identify major characteristics of the historical development of Korea during ancient, medieval, modern and contemporary periods.

3. The students should be able to conduct more in-depth research on Korean history, and also explore the relationship between Korea and other major powers in Asia, including China, Japan, the US and Russia (formerly the Soviet Union) since the twentieth century.

1. 學生能夠敘述及分析韓國的歷史發展過程，並解釋影響韓國歷史發展的重要因素。

2. 學生能夠辨別韓國在古代、中古時代、現代及當代歷史發展的特點。

3. 學生能夠對韓國歷史進行更深入的研究，並了解自二十世紀以來韓國與主要影響亞洲地區發展的國家，包括中國、日本、美國，以及俄羅斯 (前蘇聯) 的關係。

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Leadership Lessons from History
courses.description: History is full of examples of leaders faced with challenges that mirror the modern world. In this course, we will consider the lessons for leadership offered by a variety of historical figures, with a focus on ancient Greece and Rome. By balancing historical specificity with universal applicability, this course will teach students about both the past and the present. This course will also give an opportunity for working on communication skills. There is no final paper. Instead, students will complete a multimedia project (either Tableau project or scholarly video documentary, both with accompanying text commentaries).
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. To understand the principles of effective leadership from historical examples.
2. Understand ethnical issues inherent in leadership roles through historical examples.
3. Improve communication skills applicable to leadership roles, including using digital technologies.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Local History and Public History
courses.description: This course examines the history of Hong Kong from a public history perspective. Chronologically and thematically organized, its lectures examines the places, peoples, and cultures of Hong Kong from the ancient period up to the present in the major fields of public history. These fields include archaeology, oral history, popular culture, public museums, archives, cultural heritage, and digital history. This course will make extensive use of historical images, videos, oral records, antiquities, monuments, and scholarly writings on local history and public history.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken HIST2501
courses.learning_outcomes:
• To identify the major themes and topics pertaining to the local history and public history of Hong Kong

• To appreciate how, in the fields of local history and public history, Hong Kong is related to Mainland China and other parts of the world

• To understand how history is written based on our contemporary understanding of and interest in the past

• To develop among the students skills to conduct research and produce writings on local history as a public historian

• 掌握與香港本地史學和公眾史學相關之主要課題

courses.description: This course analyzes the characteristics of the Wei-Jin era with special emphasis on political upheavals, social, economic, cultural and institutional changes. Topics also cover the examination of historical literature, inscriptions and archaeological relics.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Social and Cultural History of Song China
courses.description: The Song dynasty has been acclaimed by its culture in Chinese history. Song culture originated from the aristocratic and military society of the Tang and Five Dynasties (~7th-10th centuries) and paved the way for the proliferation of educated shi-elites and lineage system in the successive Yuan and Ming dynasties (~13th-17th centuries). Given the principal position of Song dynasty in Chinese history, it is of particular importance to explore Song culture and society, as well as their influence and interaction with the foreign dynasties in northern China. Chinese culture in the future does not necessarily follows the Song pattern. Nonetheless, Song culture and society still deserves the keen attention of modern Chinese.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Intellectual Landscape of the Middle Periods of China
courses.description: Since the second half of the eighth century, China underwent a great transformation in terms of intellectual landscape. From the perspective of the dynasties of the Central Plain, the transition period from the late Tang to early Ming serves as a watershed in Chinese intellectual history. Through the investigation and analysis of some crucial cultural and intellectual norms during this period, this course aims to lead students into the intellectual landscape of the Middle Periods of China. Master Lu's Annals of Spring and Autumn mentions how antiquity and contemporiness are connected to each other in essence. This course attempts to provide a platform for students to comprehend the thoughts of past people. Thereby they can understand the value and meaning of studying intellectual history.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1) To understand the role played by intellectual history in histroical studies
2) To examine some basic concepts and ideas in Chinese intellecutual history through historical and philosophical lens
3) To explore the social context of the intellectual landscape of the Middle Periods of China (8th to 14th centuries)
4) To inquiry into the origins of some pre-modern Chinese thoughts

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Economy and Markets in Ancient China (Pre-Qin to Eastern Han)
courses.description: This course introduces students to the major concepts, methods, and evidence used to study markets and economic systems in early China. We begin by examining what a “market” is—both as an economic mechanism and as a social institution—and review the analytical tools that historians, archaeologists, and anthropologists employ to investigate ancient economies. The course surveys a wide range of materials that reveal the operation of early markets, including textual sources, archaeological remains, marketplace layouts, craft production sites, and early forms of currency. By drawing on these different types of evidence, students will gain a comprehensive understanding of how economic institutions developed from the Zhou period through the Qin and Han empires, and how market systems took shape within the broader political and social landscape of early China. Throughout the semester, students will also be introduced to recent scholarship and new discoveries that have reshaped long-standing interpretations. The course encourages critical reassessment of traditional narratives—such as the presumed decline of the Eastern Han economy—by closely engaging with excavated documents, historical records, and updated archaeological findings. By the end of the course, students will be able to evaluate competing interpretations, understand how different types of evidence contribute to economic history, and situate early Chinese markets within wider debates about state power, urbanism, and economic development.
courses.learning_outcomes:
* Develop a foundational understanding of the economic history of early China, from early dynastic redistributive systems to the formation of Qin–Han market institutions, and grasp the long-term evolution of these economic structures.
* Analyze textual sources—including bronze inscriptions, bamboo manuscripts, and transmitted historical works—related to markets, exchange, currency, and state administration, and interpret these materials with critical awareness of their historical contexts.
* Apply interdisciplinary perspectives, especially anthropological theories such as embeddedness, social networks, and institutional analysis, to understand the political, social, and cultural roles of markets in early China.
* Integrate theoretical approaches, textual evidence, and archaeological materials to examine how market and monopoly systems gradually developed and how they were connected to broader early economic patterns.
* Recognize how these early economic formations influenced subsequent institutional traditions and place ancient Chinese economic systems within a long-term and comparative historical framework.
* Understand the structural importance of markets within Chinese history and evaluate their significance in shaping later economic and state practices.
* 了解古代中國經濟史的基本發展脈絡，從早期王朝的再分配體系到秦漢市場制度的建立，並掌握其長時段的制度演變。
* 能分析金文、簡牘與傳世文獻中與市場、交易、貨幣、國家管理等相關的材料，並以批判性的方式判讀其歷史背景。
* 掌握跨學科視角，特別是運用人類學概念，如嵌入性（embeddedness）、社會網絡與制度分析，來理解市場在政治、社會與文化層面的角色。
* 能整合理論、文獻與考古證據，探討市場與專賣制度在早期中國如何逐步形成，並理解它們與不同經濟模式之間的互動關係。
* 能評估早期經濟制度對後世中國制度傳統的塑造方式，並從長時段與比較視角理解市場在中國歷史中的結構性重要性。
* 理解市場在中國歷史發展中的結構性地位，並評估其在後世經濟運作與國家制度實踐形成過程中的關鍵作用。
courses.course_syllabus:
Week 1 — Introduction: How to Study the Economic History of Early China
Theme: The food-and-goods (shihuo) system in early China and basic approaches to economic research.

Week 2 — What Is an Ancient “Market”? Concepts, Definitions, and Methods
Theme: How to identify market institutions and interpret relevant evidence from archaeological materials.

Week 3 — Production, Consumption, and Redistribution in Early States (Erlitou and the Shang)
Theme: Can the centrally organized production of early states be regarded as an early form of “commodity economy”?

Week 4 — Shell Money and Equivalency Exchange Mechanisms in Early States (Erlitou and the Shang)
Theme: Can shell valuables be considered the earliest form of money in China?

Week 5 — The Ritual Economy of the Western Zhou and the Emergence of Proto-Market Institutions
Theme: The development of commodity exchange in the Western Zhou and the earliest evidence of market institutions.

Week 6 — Urbanization in the Eastern Zhou and the Rise of Market Districts
Theme: Urbanization trends during the Eastern Zhou and the formation of market networks.

Week 7 — Standardization of Coinage and the Institutionalization of the Commodity Economy in the Eastern Zhou
Theme: How the standardization of coinage promoted the development of Eastern Zhou market institutions.

Week 8 — State Intervention in Warring States Markets and the Qin Policy of “Prioritizing Agriculture over Commerce”
Theme: The interaction between market development and state policies from the Warring States to the Qin.

Week 9 — The Spatial Organization of Markets and Urban Politics in the Han Dynasty
Theme: How marketplaces in Han urban centers were organized, planned, and administered.

Week 10 — Western Han Salt and Iron Monopolies and the Food-and-Goods System
Theme: The operational mechanisms and underlying logic of monopoly policies in the Western Han Empire.

Week 11 — Transformations in the Western Han Craft-Official System and the Expansion of Local Markets in the Eastern Han
Theme: What major changes occurred in the economic system from the Western Han to the Eastern Han?

Week 12 — The Trading Networks of Eastern Han Linxiang and Challenges to the “Natural Economy” Narrative
Theme: Insights into Eastern Han local markets and commercial activities through the Linxiang bamboo-strip documents.

Week 13 — The Long-Term Perspective on Eastern Han Market Economies: Evolving Relations Between Market and State
Theme: The impact of Eastern Han market development on later institutions and state governance.

第 1 週 — 導論：如何研究古代中國經濟史
主題：早期中國的食貨體系與經濟研究的基本方法

第 2 週—什麼是古代的「市場」？概念、定義與研究方法

第5週—早期王朝 (西周) 禮制經濟與原始市場制度的出現
主題: 西周時期商品交換的發展與最早市場制度的相關證據

第6週—東周城市化與市場區的興起
主題: 東周時期的城市化趨勢與市場網絡的形成

第7週—東周鑄幣與商品經濟的制度化
主題: 鑄幣的規範化如何推動東周市場制度的發展

第8週—戰國市場的國家干預與秦「重農抑商」問題
主題: 戰國至秦時期市場發展與國家政策之間的互動

第 9 週 —漢代的市場的空間與城市政治
主題: 漢代城市中的市場如何被組織、規劃與管理

第10週—西漢的鹽鐵壟斷與食貨經濟體系
主題: 西漢帝國壟斷政策的運作模式與其背後邏輯

第11週—西漢工官體系之轉變與東漢地方市場的擴張
主題: 西漢至東漢的經濟體系產生了哪些重要轉變？

第 12 週—東漢臨湘地區的交易網絡與「自然經濟」論之挑戰
主題: 從臨湘簡牘資料觀察東漢地方市場與商業活動

第13週 —東漢市場經濟的長時段視角：市場—國家關係的演變
主題: 東漢市場經濟發展對後世制度與國家治理的影響

courses.description: This course introduces the panorama of economics and social development on medieval England from William the Conqueror to late medieval period. Different aspects will be discussed in this course, such as social structures, urban development, lay piety and women status.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students should be obtain the following knowledge after this course:

1. a general understading on medieval England social history;
2. the development on England economic structure;
3. critical thoughts on comparing England to other countries in the same period.

3. 比較英國社會和其他同時期國家之不同。

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The French Revolution
courses.description: The French Revolution was one of the major transformational events of European History. It therefore deserves a place in any historical curriculum.It shows both the power of ideas to shape events and the ability of events to transcend the ideas that originally inspired them. The Revolution also reshaped European politics outside of France, through the series of wars that took place both during the Revolution and during the subsequent Napoleonic era.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken HIST4306
courses.learning_outcomes:
1) The basic narrative of events in France, 1789-1799

2) The general outline of the historiographical debate about the causes of the Revolution and the causes of its

radicalization

3) The key leaders of the Revolution

4) The Revolution's impact on the rest of Europe

In addition, the course would focus on the following skills

1) working with primary texts from the era

2) evaluating competing interpretations

1) 1789-1799年間法國發生的重要事件

2) 從歷史爭論中勾勒革命的源起及極端主義的興起由來

3) 法國大革命的重要領導者

4) 法國大革命對歐洲的影響

本課程並著重以下的技巧
1) 對法國大革命時代的原始文本進行探索

2) 評論對法國大革命的不同見解

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Colonial and Revolutionary America
courses.description: The course will begin with a discussion of the arrival of Europeans in North America and the development of English colonies in North America and, to a lesser extent, the West Indies. It will continue with the development of colonial society with an emphasis on the role of race relations; the different dynamics in each colony; and the importance of slavery. The second part of the course will go over the deterioration of relations between England and its American colonies, the importance of Republicanism in shaping colonists' self-understanding, before shifting to the Declaration of Independence and the course of the war with England, before moving on to the formulation of the U.S. Constitution and the debates between the Federalists and the Anti-Federalists.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1) The basic narrative of events in North America from its "discovery" until the 1790s

2) The general outline of the historiographical debate about the causes of the American Revolution

3) The key leaders of Colonial Society and of the Revolution

4) The role of Republicanism in the American Revolution

5) The role of racial relations in American society

In addition, the course would focus on the following skills

1) working with primary texts from the era

2) evaluating competing interpretations

１）對一九七零年代以前北美的情況與開發有基本認識
２）認識歷史學界對於美國革命成因的學術爭論
３）探討殖民協會的主要領導人物及其革命
４）探討共和主義在美國革命中所扮演的角色
５）探討種族關係在美國社會中所扮演的角色

此外，本課程會集中訓練以下的史學技巧：
１）運用課程探討年代的原始史料
２）處理和評估對立的論述

courses.description: This course will focus on the emergence and development of the Early Modern Atlantic World. courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Traditional Japan
courses.description:
This course introduces the Japanese tradition from late 8th century to mid-nineteenth centuries. Students will learn how the “Japanese-ness” developed in the Edo closed foreign policy, and how and why some traditions still survive today.
In each lecture, one traditional form of arts, crafts, ritual, festival or lifestyle is introduced, with its historical background. How did the tradition start, transformed, sustained or disappeared? What are the interpretation, image and importance of tradition in contemporary world, and why? The course aims to analyze Japanese culture and society through examining the historical development of tradition.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken HIST3213 and HIST5507F.
courses.learning_outcomes:
- Understand the transformation of Japanese traditional culture before the Meiji Restoration / Westernisation

- Gain the knowledge on Japanese study resources

- Develop the comparative view on traditional and imported cultures in the historical context

- Train the research, academic writing and editing skill through reading and essay assignments

- 明瞭明治維新或西化時期以前日本傳統文化的變革；

- 汲取有關日本研究資訊的知識；

- 養成對悠久歷史背景下的傳統的、外來的諸種文化的比較視野；

- 透過閱讀和論文作業，鍛鍊研究、撰寫和改訂學術著作的技巧。

courses.description: It is important to understand the emergence of Japan from a relatively isolated feudal society into the second largest economic power in the world after the US. It is the only society that successfully modernized prior to the 1970’s, and it is the only country in Asia that belongs to the G7. It has had a significant economic impact upon its neighbors as well as the world.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: War and Society (1000-1900)
courses.description: This course studies how societies make war and how war affects societies. The focus is not so much about military strategy, but more on the interaction among wars, technological innovation and institutional evolution. It mainly studies wars in Chinese history but will also cover non-Chinese historical episodes.
courses.learning_outcomes:
- Rethinking history from the perspective of war.

- Abandon the popular obsession about military strategy, instead, develop a social-history approach to the study of war.

- Develop critical judgement on war-related issues like war and peace, war and justice, individual freedom and collective well-being, nationalism and jingoism.

- 從軍事的角度思考歷史；

- 去除對於軍事戰略的迷戀，以社會史的角度研究戰爭歷史；

- 深入思考戰爭與和平、戰爭與公義、個人自由與集體福利、民族主義與軍國主義等問題。
courses.course_syllabus:

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Gender and History
courses.description: This course demonstrates critically how the gender perspective as an important new academic paradigm challenges the mainstream historical analysis and explanation and influences feminist historiography. Topics may vary from year to year based on the respective teacher's research specialization in women's/Gender History of China, Asia, or the West.
courses.learning_outcomes:
修畢本科後，學生當能：
1. 認識性別史對主流歷史分析和解釋的挑戰，及對女性主義史學的影響。

2. 了解任教老師按其研究專長定出的婦女/ 性別史專題內容。

3. 掌握以上有關歷史課題的性別觀，從兩性權力關係及其歷史語境的複雜性切入，對重要問題作出批判分析。

4. 透過對有關論著的闡釋研讀，引發概念、方法、史料、論述等方面的反思。

5. 對有關歷史課題作口頭和文字報告。

6. 在作業中展示對婦女/ 性別史課題的綜合、說明和解釋能力以及研究潛力。
courses.course_syllabus:
討論重點
近年之討論重點為中國現代國家建構之性別觀，從兩性權力關係及其歷史語境之複雜性切入，對婦女在廿世紀中國現代民族國家建構過程中各階段之經驗及處境作歷史闡釋，並透過對有關論著之闡釋研讀，引發研究方法、史料、論述等方面之反思。

討論專題及閱讀材料
節數 專題
一 導論：性別與歷史研究新範式
二 婦女史與性別史之論爭
三 中國歷史之婦女史及性別史研究進路
四 中國民族主義之性別觀﹕早期中國女權運動及其男性倡導者
五 從「國民之母」到「女國民」
六 「新女性」﹕女性與新文化運動
七 現代性之性別觀：民國時期之婦女議題
八 中國革命之性別觀
九 「國家女性主義」﹕毛澤東時代之婦女
十 改革開放之性別意涵
十一 「新女性主義」前後的台灣婦女運動
十二 婦女、性別與殖民地國家及社會﹕香港一例
十三 中外學者研究方向總評

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Revolutions: East and West
courses.description: This is a team-taught course exploring major revolutions in East and West since the eighteenth century. Different perspectives on the various resolutions will be examined, as well as comparisons and contrasts among the chosen revolutions. The lectures will introduce students to the types of questions historians ask, as well as to the multiple and often contradictory answers which different historians offer to these questions. The contents may vary from year to year.
courses.learning_outcomes:
- Deepening the understanding of history through primary sources

- Developing critical thinking through analysis of historical materials on the revolutions of different countries

- Compare the essence of historical studies of different countries

- Learning basic skills in writing history research reports and enhancing writing ability.

- Cultivating an interest in engaging in historical research in the future

- 透過原始資料加深對歷史的認識

- 透過分析不同國家的革命史料建立批判思維

- 比較對不同國家的歷史研究的精粹

- 學習撰寫歷史研究報告的基礎知識從而改善寫作能力

- 培養學生將來研究歷史的興趣

courses.title: History, Memory, and Monuments
courses.description: History, Memory, and Monuments offers a new frame for learners to expand their comprehension of how historical knowledge is formed, and how it is consumed within the arena of public spaces and the viewing of monument. In particular, the course examines how monuments/heritage sites, alongside museums, etc., function as gatekeepers of historical knowledge and as channels of social memory. The course, thus, breaks down dynamics (both local and global) that contribute to public debate about the past. In amalgamating knowledge of representations of the past with the development of skills in historical methodology, theory, and practice, students can expand cognisance as to how public history is represented, constructed, debated and, at times, contested. By possessing new critical awareness and skills students will be better able to sense and value the variety of roles played by historians in public settings, and the significance and impact too of public history upon culture, politics, and society at large.

courses.title: Iconographies, Unearthed Documents and Qin-Han History
courses.description: This course examines the iconographies of Han bricks, Han stones, and the documents of bamboo slips/wooden tablets. In reference to the primary sources, the topics of the study will cover the symbolic meanings of Han iconographies, the political and social implications of the documents concerned.
courses.learning_outcomes:
- Learn to use the solid knowledge of unearthed documents, such bamboo slips to study the history of Qin-Han China.

- Understand the history of Han China through the study of Han iconographies.

- Develop critical thinking by examining some of the conventional wisdoms in the study of Chinese history.

- Grasp presentation skills through discussion in tutorials.

- 學習利用出土文書，例如秦漢簡牘以瞭解秦漢時代的歷史。

- 透過探討漢代圖像材料認識漢代歷史。

- 透過考察中國歷史的問題以培養批判思維。

- 透過導修課學習書面及口頭報告的技巧。

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Material Culture in Ancient China
courses.description:
This course presents a comprehensive introduction to Pre-Han China focusing on thrilling archaeological discoveries. The course places emphasis on social, political and economic aspects of ancient China and major social transitions reflected in material cultures in order to complement the missing of textual records. We will examine a variety of themes through the lens of material culture engaged with primary and secondary textual sources. We cover the period between the transition of Neolithic and early domestication until the end of the Qin Empire. The main focus is on understanding how we can reconstruct various aspects of ancient China through the analysis and interpretation of material culture.
Important themes covered in the class include the origin and foundation of early civilization, the formation of early state, urbanism, divination and state-sponsored ritual, trade and core-periphery relations, craft industry and technological change, the emergence of state bureaucracies, and the process of political unification. The course will provide students a basic understanding of these topics in the contexts of early China as understand through the material culture of ancient Chinese societies in juxtaposition with early textual sources including oracle bone inscription and bronze inscriptions. Weekly tutorial sections will focus on the implications and significance of these themes.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken HIST4140
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this course, students are expected to:

• Analyze the formation process of civilization and major transformative social changes in ancient China.

• Understand how archaeologists reconstruct the history of “prehistory” through archaeological records.

• Critically evaluation the strength and limitation in archaeological research.

• Discuss how archaeological records can be productively supplement textual evidence in historical research.

• Understand the legacy of big social changes and impacts of ancient China in present-day societies.

• Cultivate the abilities of cross-cultural, inter-disciplinary and critical thinking.

預期達到的教學目的包括:

- 分析早期中國文明的形成過程和重大社會轉折

- 如何以考古材料重建“史前史”

- 對考古研究優點和局限之批判性分析能力

- 在歷史學研究中如何以考古資料有效地輔助文獻研究

- 早期中國在當代社會的深遠影響

- 跨文化與跨學科之研究能力

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Imperial Capitals: Chang'an, Luoyang and Kaifeng (BCE 202 - 1130 CE)
courses.description: This course is a survey of the evolution of imperial capitals of Chang’an, Luoyang and Kaifeng in natural geography, city planning, metropolitan area, society, economy and military defense during a period of about one millennium from the Middle Ages to the early modern times. In particular, the ecology, topography, morphology, social structure and control, security, street and market system, industrial and commercial network, religious and cultural life of the capitals, and the interactions among them will be analyzed with a comparative approach. This course will also deal with the systems of imperial mausoleum, granary, grain transport, taxes, corvee, land tenure, administration, monitoring, traffic, boundary pass and military affairs in metropolitan areas, and the transformation of a dual capital system into a multiple capital system. Through PowerPoint lectures and interactive tutorials on these topics, students will thoroughly understand the structural transformation and relocation trend of the national capital in North China during this period. Teacher will also provide guidance in reading the related written sources and archaeological finds useful for writing the term paper.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who had taken HIST4309
courses.course_syllabus:
A. Topics on capitals

1. Location, ecology and topography of capitals

It analyses the basic factors affecting the location of traditional capitals, their ecology and problems of natural disasters.

2. Morphology and city planning of capitals (1)

It traces the origin of traditional capitals in China, investigates the layout of Capital Xianyang and the temporary palaces away from the capital in the Qin dynasty, and explores the transformation of morphology and city planning of the capitals of Changan, Luoyang and Kaifeng from the Han to the Song dynasty, especially the change of location of their palace cities from facing the east to facing the south.

3. Morphology and city planning of capitals (2)

It investigates the morphology and city planning of the T’ang capitals of Chang’an and Luoyang and the Song capital of Kaifeng and evaluates the impact of the T’ang capitals on the capital planning of other countries in East Asia.

4. Social structure, market system and commercial activities in capitals (1)

It explores the social structure, market system and commercial activities in Capital Luoyang in Northern Wei dynasty and Capital Chang’an in the T’ang dynasty.

5. Social structure, market system and commercial activities in capitals (2)

It explores the social structure, market system and commercial activities in Capital Kaifeng in Northern Song dynasty

6. Daily life, religion and cultural intercourse in capitals

It illustrates the food culture, sports, entertainments, international cultural exchange activities and spread of foreign religions especially Nestorianism in Capital Chang’an in the T’ang dynasty.

B. Topics on metropolitan areas

7. The origin, scope, bureaucracy, administration and monitoring of metropolitan areas (1)

It explains the demarcation of metropolitan areas by the Western Zhou dynasty which commenced the metropolitan system in China, and explores the evolution of metropolitan areas since the Qin dynasty.

8. The origin, scope, bureaucracy, administration and monitoring of metropolitan areas (2)

It explores the development of metropolitan areas in the T’ang and Northern Song dynasties and demonstrates the special bureaucracy, administration and monitoring systems in there.

9. The systems of tax, corvée and land tenure in metropolitan areas

It shows that the metropolitan areas had been establishing as both the centre of tax and corvée and the income base for the emperor and the central government officials by prohibiting migration of the registered population, feudalization and hunting in the areas, and allocating the land (rent) there to the central officials from the Western Zhou dynasty through the T’ang dynasty.

10. The post roads and boundary passes for defense in metropolitan areas

It illustrates the facilities of postal stations and the post road transport in the metropolitan areas from the Western Zhou dynasty through the Song dynasty. It particularly explores the systems of post road transport and four-side boundary passes in the east and west metropolitan areas in the Han and T’ang dynasties.

11. Temporary palaces and military affairs in metropolitan areas

It explores the history of metropolitan areas serving as the military centre of the Empire and especially the high concentration of militia units and temporary palaces in the two metropolitan areas in the Sui-T’ang dynasties.

C. Topics on capital system

12. The systems of dual capitals and multiple capitals

It examines the development of sub-capital system from the Xia dynasty to the Song dynasty and its determining factors. It particularly explores the evolution of the dual capital system to multiple capital system and the official system of branch offices in Capital Luoyang in the T’ang dynasty.

13. The relocation trend of the national capital and its determining factors

It analyses the eastward relocation trend of the national capital and its determining factors from the Sui dynasty to the Northern Song dynasty.

一. 都城篇

1. 都城之選址與生態形勢

本課分析古代都城選址的基本因素、古都的生態環境，以及都城的災害問題。

2. 都城之城郭形制與規劃結構 (1)

本課追溯中國都城的起源，考察秦都咸陽城及離宮的佈局，探討漢至宋朝的長安、洛陽、開封三都的城郭形制和規劃結構之演變，尤其西漢都城宮殿坐西朝東的形制和東漢以後宮殿坐北朝南的形制。

3. 都城之城郭形制與規劃結構 (2)

本課探討唐朝長安、洛陽兩都及宋朝開封都城的城郭形制、規劃結構，以及唐兩都對古代東亞國家的都城規劃的影響。

4. 都城之社會結構、市制及商業活動 (1)

本課分析北魏洛陽和唐代長安兩都的社會結構、市制及商業活動。

5. 都城之社會結構、市制及商業活動 (2)

本課分析北宋開封都城的社會結構、市制及商業活動。

6. 都城之生活、宗教及文化交流

本課探討唐朝長安都城市民的飲食文化、體育娛樂，以及城中的國際文化交流活動和外來宗教如景教的傳播發展。

二. 都畿篇

7. 畿內之起源、範圍演變及官僚體系和行政、監察制度 (1)

本課考察西周王畿的建立，說明中國畿內制的起源，並探討秦朝以降歷代王朝的畿內範圍之演變。

8. 畿內之起源、範圍演變及官僚體系和行政、監察制度 (2)

本課考察唐朝和北宋的畿內演變及其特殊的官僚體系和行政、監察制度。

9. 都畿之土地及賦役制度

本課說明從西周至唐朝，畿內充當天子的供御地和京官的租入地，限制所在編戶遷往畿外，常予賦役的減免優待，又禁止分封諸侯和戈獵採捕，而將土地(田租)授予京官。

10. 都畿之驛道交通與關防

本課探討西周至宋朝的畿內郵驛交通制度，尤其說明漢、唐兩朝東、西兩畿的驛道和四面關制度。

11. 都畿之離宮與軍事部署

本課考察古代王朝畿內充當軍事基地的傳統，尤其著重說明隋唐兩朝京畿所在密集的皇帝離宮和軍府部署。

三. 都制篇

12. 兩都制與數都制

本課考察上古夏朝至宋朝的陪都制度發展及相關因素，尤其深入討論隋唐兩朝從兩都制演變到數都制的發展，以及唐朝東都的分司官體制。

13. 國都的遷移趨勢及其因素

本課分析隋至宋朝期間國都東移的趨勢及其基本因素。

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Industrial Revolution and Its Impacts
courses.description:
The module intends to provide a survey of the origins and transformations of industrial society over the last two centuries or so, a period of time within which industrial nation states have reached new heights of power and acquired the dominant share of the world’s wealth – a wealth once dominated by Westerners but increasingly challenged in recent years by the rise of, for example, South East Asian nations. This comparative studies programme shall allow students to obtain a critical understanding of the nature of industrial society through fostering a multidisciplinary approach to industrialisation and many of the changes in society it helped to establish. The course will give students the opportunity to consider the ideas and the conditions in Europe and elsewhere that produced industrial change, capitalism and democracy – processes that the West considered then and still considers today as desirable for itself and other parts of the world. The curriculum gives particular focus to pre-industrial Europe and its economy, industrial Britain, urbanisation and its effects upon social classes, public health, housing and ways of living. The course is designed to build skills such as thinking critically, well-constructed writing and the clear presenting of oral arguments. In so doing students will be expected to critically engage with a range of academic disciplines such as History (social and economic, cultural and urban), Social Studies, Economics and Geography, so as to answer questions such as:

• In what ways did industrialisation fundamentally change societies?
• What factors accounted for the beginning of the Industrial Revolution?
• How did patterns of urbanisation change as a consequence of industrial growth?
• How did social class relations shift due to industrial progress?
• How did industrial changes affect the role of women or children in the work place?
• What demographic changes have occurred since industrialisation began?
• Were the First and Second Industrial Revolutions the same or were they different?
• How did rural developments affect the rise of industry in Europe’s past?
• What is the relationship between cities and the countryside both before and after the onset of industrial growth?
• What dangers arise from industrial and urban transition? Are these dangers universal?
courses.learning_outcomes:
At the end of the course students should be able to achieve the following objectives:

1. Recognise and explain key events that led to upheavals within the economies and societies of Europe, North America and Asia, in so doing enhancing existing knowledge of what shaped these continents.

2. Grasp the relationship between the evolution of industrialisation and the changing nature of societies.

3. Consider broad issues within History in greater depth so as to make connections between industrial growth and other contexts.

4. Demonstrate historical knowledge via a short tutorial presentation and class-centred exercises.

5. Exhibit critical thinking and research skills through the writing of scholarly assignments and the compiling of an online portfolio.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: West and the World III: Early Modernity
courses.description: The early modern period (c. 1400-1800 CE) was highly formative for modern (i.e industrial and post-industrial) “Western” societies, featuring the beginnings of modern European politics, culture, religion, science, colonialism, etc. This course will have two aims: to understand the continuities and innovations during the early modern period of “Western” history, and to understand its relationship to the rest of the world (Ming-Qing China, India, the Americas, Africa, etc.). This course will also feature a visit to the CUHK Rare Book Collection to examine early modern printed books.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken HIST4306
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Develop an understanding of the middle period of Western history.

2. Develop a critical understanding of the commenalities and connections between East and West.

3. Learn to critically analyze sources and documents, and develop critical thinking skills.

4. Engage with real primary sources (rare books).

1. 瞭解西方歷史的中間階段

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: A Tale of Three Cities: Hong Kong, Shanghai and Singapore
courses.description: This course examines and compares the historical development of three Asian cities - Shanghai, Hong Kong and Singapore, focusing on the impact of Western colonialism and Chinese cultural traditions on the socio-economic growth and politico-cultural transformation of the cities.
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of the course, students will:

(1) have gained a solid training in empirical methods for the historical studies of Shanghai, Hong Kong and Singapore

(2) have developed critical thinking in analyzing the impact of Western colonialism and Chinese traditions on the socio-economic growth and politico-cultural transformation of these cities

修讀本科後，學生當能:

(1) 掌握實證方法研習上海、香港和新加坡的歷史發展

(2) 批判思考西方殖民主義及華人傳統文化對當地工商業發展及城市政治和文化的影響

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Christianity in World History
courses.description: This course charts the major stages in the history of Christianity from its origins in the Roman Empire to the present day. It also looks at a range of themes, including the relationship between religion and politics, the role of religion in shaping cultural identities, different expressions of religious spirituality, and the confrontation between religion and secularism.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. To introduce students to the historical development of Christianity around the world: key dates, places, events, processes, writings, etc.

2. To familiarise students with the most important themes and scholarly debates in the history of world Christianity.

3. To help students develop the skillset and sensibility of a historian: how to understand primary sources, think critically about historical questions, and communicate their analysis to others.

1. 讓同學掌握基督宗教在世界各地的歷史梗概：重要的日期、地點、事件、史料等。

2. 讓同學掌握史學界對世界歷史上基督宗教的主要研究觀點和論辯。

3. 讓同學掌握歷史學家的技藝與敏銳觸覺：如何解讀原始史料、如何就歷史問題進行批判性思維、如何表達自己的觀點。
courses.course_syllabus:
1. Introduction: Religious Belief in the Ancient World

2. The First Christians

3. A Christian Roman Empire

4. Beyond the Roman World: The 'Oriental Churches'

5. The Conversion of Northern Europe

6. Byzantium and the Slavs

7. The Papal Monarchy

8. East and West: The 'Great Schism'

9. Heresy and Inquisition

10. Reformation and Counter-Reformation

11. Global Empires and Christian Missions

12. The Enlightenment Challenge

13. Epilogue: Christianity in the Modern World

1. 導論：上古歷史上的宗教信仰

2. 早期基督徒

3. 皈依基督的羅馬帝國

4. 羅馬帝國勢力以外：所謂「東方教會」

5. 北歐皈依基督

6. 拜占庭與斯拉夫民族

7. 教廷

8. 東與西：大分裂

9. 異端與宗教裁判所

10. 宗教改革與反改革

11. 寰球帝國與傳教使命

12. 啟蒙運動的挑戰

13. 終章：現代的基督宗教

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Qing History
courses.description: The course introduces the History of Qing dynasty (1644-1911), with an emphasis on the transformation of China from an empire to a nation, and in this process, how the Manchus and the Hans identifi ed themselves ethnically.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For all PG prog in Division of History
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking the course, the students should be able to learn about:
(1) The ethnicity of Jushen, Manchu and Manzu
(2) Governance of Qing Government
(3) Formation of village armed forces in mid-Qing
(4) From Empire to Nation
(5) Development of firearms

透過此課程，學生應能學習到：
(1) 從女真人，到滿洲人，到滿族人的族群身份建構過程。
(2) 滿清的統治政策。
(3) 清中葉農村武裝力量形成的原因。
(4) 中國由帝國轉變到民族國家的經過。
(5) 火器的演變。

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Pearl River Delta 1368-1911
courses.description: The course introduces, in the Ming and Qing periods, how local society in the Pearl River Delta was integrated into the Chinese state through a series of changes that involved constant redefinition of lineages, territories, and ethnic identities.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For all PG prog in Division of History
courses.learning_outcomes:
To learn about the historical development of Pearl River Delta from the Song dynasty to the Republic；
To learn to combine field work experience with documentary research in understanding local history;
To appreciate that ethnic and local identities, such as Yao, Miao, Hakka or boat people, were constructed in historical contexts;
To be sensitive to how, in different historical periods, local societies negotiated with government agencies in the implementation of financial, cultural, educational policies, and how such negotiations contributed to ethnic and local identities.

1 瞭解自宋至民國時期珠江三角洲的歷史發展，從長時段的角度看歷史；
2 學習結合田野資料和體驗，解讀特定地點的歷史資料；
2 通過對地方社會中人群的不同身份討論，瞭解身份的形成與變動是一個歷史過程。
3 瞭解不同時期，地方社會如何與政府制度打交道，比如財政、文化、教育等等。這個過程如何影響族群與身份認同。

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Science and Civilization in Early China: Lithic and Jade Technology
courses.description: The history of technology is one of the important components of civilization; it is also the main impetus to its development. In particular, ancient Chinese technology has made vital contributions to the world civilization. This course will include lectures, jades manufacture experiment and examination, also, archaeological sites and museum visit. It is aimed at introducing the process and features of the formation of human lives and civilization in China and East Asian region through the history of lithic and jade technology.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For all PG prog in Division of History
courses.learning_outcomes:
Deepen students' understanding of Science and Civilization in Early China
Build up learning interest as a lifelong process
Develop critical thinking through analysis on historical materials

courses.description: The course is divided into three parts. Part I introduces the history of museum development, major theoretical literature on museums, and current issues in museology. courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Cross-Strait Relations in International and Historical Perspectives
courses.description: This course examines the history of the relationship between Taiwan and mainland China since the end of World War II, when Taiwan ceased to be a Japanese colony. The victory of the Communists in China's civil war in 1949 and the relocation of the Kuomintang Government to Taipei sparked off the dispute over Taiwan's status, which endures to the present day. Now President Chen Shui-bian wants to redefine Taiwan's status as a sovereign, independent country whose name is the Republic of China, while Beijing defines Taiwan as part of China. This course will examine the stand taken on Taiwan by key international actors, in particular the United States, but including Japan and the European Union. It will look at the Taiwan Straits military crises of the 1950s and the role of the United States, the initial strong international support for the KMT government as the sole legal government of all China until the tide turned in 1971, with Beijing replacing Taipei in the United Nations. It will also examine various international documents that have a bearing on the international status of Taiwan as well as statements issued by the government in Taiwan and leading political parties there as well as white papers on Taiwan issued by the People's Republic of China.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Festival and Popular Religion in Modern China
courses.description: This course attempts to understand Modern Chinese local societies’ social structure, principles of organization, ethnic relations and process of social change through an analysis and interpretation of festivals and popular religion. The course is divided into two parts: the first part, from a macro perspective, discusses the “position” of festivals and popular religion in the Chinese Imperial State and local society. We will try to discuss (1) how did the Ming Qing Government sanction and control local ritual activities? (2) How did different social groups depict festivals and popular religion in different periods of time? And (3) How did local society utilize the State language to enhance, adjust, reconstruct and forget local traditions? The second part, through case studies, will investigate local social activities’ organizational method and its changes in order to understand the interactive relationship between tradition and modernization. It also attempts to explore the relationship between historical narration and interpretation from analyses of these case studies.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For all PG prog in Division of History
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking the course, the students should be able to understand Modern Chinese local societies' social structure, principles of organization, ethnic relations and process of social change through an analysis and interpretation of festivals and popular religion.

courses.title: Institutions and Society in the Qing Dynasty
courses.description: (Not for students who have taken HIST5554.) The course introduces different institutions in the Qing dynasty (1644-1911), with an emphasis on the impact of these institutions on the society.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For all PG prog in Division of History
courses.learning_outcomes:
Understand the institutions of the Qing dynasty.
Understand the impact of these state institutions on the society.

理解清朝的各種制度
理解這些制度對民間社會產生何種的影響

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Archives and Hong Kong Historical Studies
courses.description: Archives are the most important information on historical research. However, archives were mainly used in the studying of political history in the past. In the twentieth century, historians have extensively used archival records in social and cultural history and gotten fruitful results. This course begins with the introduction of the research in this area. It also introduces the archives of the British colonial governance in Hong Kong and discusses how to use the archives in the research of Hong Kong History. Since the nineteenth century, Guangdong, Hong Kong, and Macao have developed a close connection in terms of politics, economy, society and culture; therefore, this course not only focuses on the archives in Hong Kong, but also introduces the collections of archives in Guangdong and Macao.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Land Administration and Practice in Hong Kong
courses.description: Land administration is the key to understand a local society. The land law in Hong Kong is consisted of two parts: (i) the application of common law on Hong Kong island and Kowloon peninsula; and (ii) the use of the Great Qing Code in the New Territories (the broad sense of the New Territories including New Kowloon). However, after the Hong Kong government has implemented the “Small House Policy” since 1972, the so-called “New Territories” does include New Kowloon. This course introduces land administration of Hong Kong (Hong Kong island, Kowloon peninsula, New Territories) from the Qing dynasty up to the present time, and how the land administration affects the livelihood of common people. With regard to basic references, the course uses Hong Kong colonial files as well as the Great Qing Code, but supplemented them with lawsuit judgments and scholarly studies.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Common People of Modern China
courses.description: This course is designed to explore the concept, the image and the livelihood of the “common people” from the last decades of the Qing dynasty to the 1940s. This era saw great changes of social and political theory: a ritual life that had reached from emperor into villages came to be articulated in relation to a central government and its cities. The rural population ceased to be central to ritual life and came to be marginalized. Orthodox values came to be looked upon as superstition. Meanwhile, a social ethos came to represent the fashion of a new age, and city life was looked upon as a symbol of progress. This transition from old to new repositioned the individual, family, nation, and even language and gender. This transition has continued to the present day, making us as much its creator as well as its product. This course seeks to raise questions about the society which we take for granted and in which we are now placed has evolved from the late Qing.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For all PG prog in Division of History
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. To become aware of the tenuousness of the idea of a “common people”
2. To apply historican knowledge to common beliefs associated with life styles that are often taken for granted.
3 To appreciate that as ideas were articulated in words, life styles were attached to them and became subjects of emulation.

1 瞭解“普通人”是一個無中生有的概念；
2 瞭解我們習以為常的生活方式以及觀念背後的歷史過程；
3 明白正如觀念與名詞的相生關係一樣，生活方式、形象也是與名詞相生的。新名詞與聯繫在一起的新形象，被創造與模仿，以至於逐漸成為了日常行為中不言而喻的部分。
courses.course_syllabus:
1. From Reform to Revolution in the making of Ah Q
2. Representing citizenship
3. The girl student: the beginning of new womanhood
4. The urban Experience
5. The transformation of work & the rise of the working class
6. The rise of popular entertainment and mass culture
7. Family and lineage
8. A gender revolution?
9. The school: intellectuals and their role in society
10. Chinese fundamentalism
11. The common people at war
12. Great men (and women) and ideologies
13. In the sweep of history: class differentiation

1. 從改革到革命的阿Q
2. 新中國的國民
3. 女學生：新婦女的開端
4. 城市經驗
5. 工作的改變與工人階級的興起
6. 普及娛樂與大眾文化
7. 家庭與宗族
8. 性別革命，有嗎？
9. 學校：知識分子與其社會責任
10. 中國式的原教旨主義
11. 抗戰中的普通人
12. 英雄與主義
13. 歷史與階級的分化
